payload.title: SECURITY: forgot-password shows the reset link on screen instead of emailing it (account takeover)
payload.body:
## Summary
Forgot-password does not email anything — it **displays the password reset link on screen**. Any visitor can enter any registered email address and immediately receive a working reset link for that account, including the admin account. This is a full account-takeover path.

## Reproduction
1. Open `/forgot-password`
2. Enter any registered email address
3. The reset link is rendered back to the browser as a flash message

## Pinpointed cause
`app/Controllers/AuthController.php:123-138`:
```php
$token = (new PasswordResetService())->createToken($email);
if ($token) {
    $link = rtrim((string)(getenv('APP_URL') ?: ''), '/') . '/reset-password?token=' . urlencode($token);
    $_SESSION['last_reset_link'] = $link;
    $this->flash('Password reset link: ' . $link, 'info');   // <-- leaked to the requester
}
```
No `MailQueueService::enqueue()` call exists anywhere in the reset flow.

Secondary defect on the same line: `getenv('APP_URL')` returns empty because `.env` is read via `parse_ini_file()` in `config/database.php` and never exported to the process environment, so the link is generated without an origin.

## Affected paths
- `app/Controllers/AuthController.php:123`
- `app/Services/PasswordResetService.php`
- `app/Services/MailQueueService.php`

## Intended scope
Enqueue the reset link by email. Never render it. Always show the same neutral response whether or not the address is registered, so the form cannot be used to enumerate accounts. Resolve `APP_URL` from config rather than `getenv()`.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Reset link never appears in the response body, flash, or session
- [ ] Identical response for registered and unregistered addresses
- [ ] Reset mail lands in `mail_queue` with an absolute URL
